title: Conceptual question
body:
Hi, if I understand it correctly, the sandbox is shipped inside the FlatImage. What security benefit does this provide?

- If you trust the FlatImage, you don't need a sandbox.
- If you don't trust the FlatImage, then you can't trust that its sandbox hasn't been tampered with.

So wouldn't it make more sense to have the sandbox outside of the FlatImage, and come directly from a trusted source (you)?

title: Applications using OpenGL segfault on the Arch image if you don't install libxkbcommon
body:
I'm getting a segfault running various OpenGL applications unless I install libxkbcommon. I'm using the 0.2.4 Arch image on a Arch host. I tried a couple of games and they all segfault.

However, if I manually install libxkbcommon, they stop segfaulting and work perfectly.

Reproduction steps:

```bash
$ ./arch.flatimage fim-resize 4G
$ ./arch.flatimage fim-perms-set wayland,pulseaudio,gpu,session_bus
$ ./arch.flatimage fim-root fakechroot pacman -S supertux --noconfirm
$ ./arch.flatimage fim-exec supertux2
# doesn't start, segfaults
$ ./arch.flatimage fim-root fakechroot pacman -S libxkbcommon --noconfirm
$ ./arch.flatimage fim-exec supertux2
# starts without problems
```

title: Integrate FlatImages better into desktop
body:
Current desktop integration only covers adding .desktop file & icon to appear into menu.

This is a nice start.

But what I see that is currently lacking is:
- support for opening links to redirect to your default web-browser & other similar scenarios (using xdg-mime)
- option to set FlatImage application to be the default (also using xdg-mime)
- support for MPRIS (media status notification)
- etc.

I believe that equivalent to these above are portals in flatpak.

If those above can be achieved when FlatImage is in portable mode, that would be great!

title: idea: Introduce concept of standardized runtimes
body:
I find that using a standardized minimal image like Alpine & layering needed application dependencies on it would be the best, in order to retain acceptable FlatImage file-size.

To make this easier, standardized runtimes would be introduced, which are similar to flatpak runtimes:

Examples:
- Mesa GPU runtime
- Gnome (GTK) runtime
- KDE (Qt) runtime
- Fontconfig runtime
- Some freedesktop runtimes
- etc.

I guess that those runtimes can be implemented as a script of install commands with grouped dependencies for each base, which would be easily visible & nicely sorted in this repo, so others can improve & fix it when necessary too.

This implementation would make things easier for developers to make & test their FlatImages for reliability before releasing them.

I know that this is easier said than done, so it's just an idea for now.

Regarding that as well, I think it could be handy to include a command that allows publishing just one image, and then easily allowing swapping the APT repositories to use a different distro (i.e. any Debian/Ubuntu release). I was thinking this could be done by hot-swapping out the config in `/etc/apt/sources.list` and then just running an `apt-get update && apt get upgrade`.

title: [Feature Request] ability to mount image and browse it using a file manager
body:
AFAIK ARTS already works by mounting to `/tmp/.mountXYZ` and then executing whatever is specified. 

Currently however it is not very convenient to edit files which are inside that image as everything needs to be done using the command line. 

Would it be possible to add the ability to just mount the image and then opening the mount path with the default file manager so that one could use that to copy / move / modify files?

I think that could be a very big QOL improvement.

PS: something like `arts-mount` would do and then open the directory using `xdg-open /path/to/mounted/image`
PPS: what exactly is the difference between `arts-exec` and `arts-root` ?
